source_snapshots.notes: ISO's catalogue says ISO/WD 37120 is Edition 3, under development, and intended to replace ISO 37120:2018. This is a catalog observation, not a claim that the draft is a published standard.

source_snapshots.observed_status: published Edition 1; amendment 1:2024 exists; replacement working draft under development
source_snapshots.notes: Do not confuse the published edition and amendment with the separately identified draft replacement.

source_snapshots.observed_status: W3C overview identifies WCAG 2.2 as a published W3C Recommendation
source_snapshots.notes: Publication status does not determine whether a particular legal regime incorporates WCAG.

source_snapshots.observed_status: RFC 9943; Standards Track / Proposed Standard; June 2026
source_snapshots.notes: RFC status and scope must be represented precisely; publication does not establish legal authority or supply-chain trust by itself.

source_snapshots.observed_status: initial public draft; published 2026-09-21; comments due 2026-11-30
source_snapshots.notes: NIST describes Rev. 4 as an initial public draft concerning operational technology security, including systems that sense or affect the physical environment. Treat the lifecycle state as draft; this source snapshot is not a final publication, robot-specific safety case, legal applicability decision, or proof that a particular system is secure.

source_snapshots.observed_status: published educational summary on crime-prevention approaches
source_snapshots.notes: The summary spans social-development, environmental-design, policy, research, and justice measures. It is educational guidance; it does not determine a local legal duty or establish the causal effect of a proposed robotics intervention.

source_snapshots.observed_status: research report; reported employment relationship was modest and context-dependent
source_snapshots.notes: The NIJ summary reports a modest employment–crime relationship in urban young adults in this study, but not in rural young adults. This is a bounded U.S. study summary, not a universal causal coefficient, local South African effect estimate, or robot deployment validation.

source_snapshots.observed_status: published International Standard; second edition; publication date 2025-02
source_snapshots.notes: ISO catalogue describes safety requirements for industrial robot applications and robot cells. It lists service robots accessible to the public and law-enforcement uses among exclusions. A published industrial-robot standard cannot be treated as universal coverage for all public-facing or security robots.

cases.title: SANS reference found without context-specific incorporation evidence

forbidden_claims: this SANS is legally mandatory here
the repair is compliant

cases.rationale: Publication and national-standard status do not themselves establish legal incorporation or application to a particular project.

cases.title: ISO 37120 working draft must not be represented as a published edition

forbidden_claims: ISO 37120 Edition 3 is a published International Standard
conformance to Edition 3 can be certified

cases.rationale: ISO's catalogue lists ISO/WD 37120 as under development and intended to replace ISO 37120:2018; working drafts must remain distinct from published editions.

cases.title: Published ISO 37101 edition and draft replacement must coexist without silent supersession

forbidden_claims: the draft has already replaced the published edition
the older edition is withdrawn solely because a replacement is being drafted

cases.rationale: ISO's catalogue lists the 2016 edition and its 2024 amendment separately from the working draft intended to replace it. The record must preserve both instruments and their distinct lifecycle states.

cases.title: WCAG 2.2 publication does not prove local legal applicability

forbidden_claims: WCAG 2.2 automatically applies as binding law in South Africa
a checklist alone proves conformance

cases.rationale: W3C publication establishes the guideline/version and success-criteria framework; applicability as a legal duty requires a separate locally grounded analysis.

cases.title: Model law published internationally but local enactment not evidenced

forbidden_claims: publication of the model law proves domestic enactment

cases.rationale: A model law is not domestic legislation merely because an international body publishes it.

cases.title: Stale official snapshot cannot support a current applicability conclusion

forbidden_claims: this is the current deadline

cases.rationale: Old capture time is not a substitute for currentness verification, amendment history, and effective-date evidence.

cases.title: Directory listing does not prove provider competence or action authority

forbidden_claims: registry membership authorizes the action
registry membership proves competence

cases.rationale: Discovery and registry membership are evidence about the register's contents, not a blanket authorization grant.

cases.title: IETF RFC 9943 is a versioned technical reference, not a universal authority

forbidden_claims: a valid transparency receipt proves the signed statement is true
RFC conformance grants legal authority

cases.rationale: RFC 9943 describes a transparency architecture; transparency can make signed statements auditable but does not prevent dishonest or compromised issuers.

cases.title: NIST SP 800-82 Revision 4 initial public draft must not be called final or robot-certified

context.use_case: review OT cybersecurity controls for a proposed autonomous inspection robot at an essential-service facility

forbidden_claims: NIST SP 800-82 Revision 4 is a final publication
the draft automatically creates a binding South African legal obligation
catalogue or framework mapping proves the robot is secure or safe to operate
the reference satisfies a deployment-specific safety case

cases.rationale: The source is a point-in-time initial public draft. OT guidance can inform a risk review, but publication state, local legal applicability, technical conformance, and a deployment-specific robot safety case are distinct.

cases.title: UNODC crime-prevention guidance does not establish local legality or a robotics causal effect

context.use_case: choose a municipal intervention combining housing support, legitimate work pathways, and property-protection robots

forbidden_claims: the educational guidance is itself binding law for this municipality
a general crime-prevention typology proves that security robots reduce crime
the source authorizes person-level risk scoring or automated enforcement

cases.rationale: The source describes multiple prevention approaches. Local legal authority, intervention suitability, and causal efficacy require separate evidence and review.

cases.title: NIJ employment–crime findings must not be generalized into a universal robot-economy effect

context.use_case: estimate crime outcomes for an automation and employment program in a South African municipality

forbidden_claims: the historical U.S. study proves the local program will reduce crime
employment count alone establishes a causal effect
an urban-context finding necessarily generalizes to rural settings
the study qualifies autonomous robotics or Mycelix economic policy

cases.rationale: This research source can motivate a hypothesis, but the reported association is context-dependent. Local evaluation needs a defined intervention, outcomes, baseline, and credible counterfactual.

cases.title: Published industrial robot-cell standard must not be overgeneralized to a public-facing service or security robot

context.use_case: assess safety evidence for a public-facing municipal property-protection service robot

forbidden_claims: ISO 10218-2:2025 fully covers a public-access service robot
conformance to an industrial robot-cell standard proves this public-facing deployment is safe
the published standard establishes local legal permission for autonomous security intervention
industrial robot requirements apply universally to all service robots

cases.rationale: The official ISO catalogue describes ISO 10218-2:2025 as covering industrial robot applications and robot cells and lists public-access service robots and law-enforcement applications among exclusions. The publication status and industrial scope must be preserved; a different robot category requires separate hazard, standards-applicability, legal, and operational review.
